thread.title: California Wildlife Officers Bust Spiny Lobster Poachers at Royal Palms Beach
thread.title_full: California Wildlife Officers Bust Spiny Lobster Poachers at Royal Palms Beach

author: Golden Gate Media
title: California Wildlife Officers Bust Spiny Lobster Poachers at Royal Palms Beach
text:
11 hours ago Los Angeles, California – California Department of Fish and Wildlife officers on coastal patrol caught four individuals illegally harvesting spiny lobsters near Royal Palms Beach in the San Pedro neighborhood of Los Angeles during the early hours of August 1.
Photo by CDFW According to the California Department of Fish and Wildlife, officers observed the suspects, dressed in wetsuits and diving gear, taking lobsters throughout the night despite the recreational and commercial season having closed months earlier in March.
The suspects attempted to flee on foot when officers made contact around 3 a.m., but all four were apprehended without incident. In the back of their vehicle, officers discovered 236 spiny lobsters, 210 of which were undersized. The individuals had no fishing licenses or required measuring devices, violations that carry multiple misdemeanor charges. “During the open lobster season, the possession limit is seven per person with a minimum size of 3 and ¼ inches measured in a straight line on the back from the rear edge of the eye socket to the rear edge of the body shell,” the California Department of Fish and Wildlife noted.
Fortunately, most of the poached lobsters were still alive and were safely returned to the ocean after officers conducted a quick count and took photographs for evidence. The four suspects were cited for taking lobster during the closed season, possessing undersized lobster, commercialization without a license, no fishing license, and no measuring device.
Authorities encourage the public to report suspicious activity to protect California’s fish and wildlife. Tips can be submitted 24/7 via CalTIP at (888) 334-2258, by texting “CALTIP” + your message to 847411, or through the CalTIP app available on Apple’s App Store and Google Play.
